text:
alex_sales: Quick heads-up — AtlasCorp POC kicks off Mon. They asked for a concrete capacity playbook: expected steady traffic, burst windows, prewarm, and impact on pricing. Can we lock down numbers today?
kevin_se: Got it. Do we have their traffic profile (RPS, typical prompt lengths, percent chat vs. embeddings)?
alex_sales: From precall: 120 RPS baseline, 800 RPS 5-min bursts (twice/day), avg prompt len ~ 80 tokens, chat ratio ~ 60%. They want reserved capacity + burst credits.
maya_prod: For that mix I'd recommend reserving capacity for 200–250 RPS to cover steady + headroom, use burst pool for the 800 spikes. Also suggest a 10–15m prewarm window before major event.
ian_sre: Reservation sizing depends on model variant. If they use a 7B quantized model, one p2-style GPU equiv handles ~400–600 RPS (80 token avg) with batching. For a 30B float model it's ~75–120 RPS. Which model are they planning?
alex_sales: They said "performance first" and prefer a 30B-ish model. Risk: cost + capacity.
olga_support: From an enterprise contract POV AtlasCorp expects an SLA for 99.9% p95 lat < 400ms. Can we meet that with reserved + burst?
maya_prod: 30B model + 99.9% p95 <400ms is tight unless we overprovision. Options: (1) Dedicated reserved GPUs sized for steady + some burst, (2) Hybrid: reserve for core 200RPS on 30B, route burst to a cheaper 7B quantized fallback with automatic fallback policy.
kevin_se: I recommend we present a cost/latency tradeoff matrix. Example config:
```
- Reserved: 4x A100-equivalent for primary 30B serving (covers ~480 RPS steady)
- Burst: autoscale pool configured up to 12 GPUs for short windows
- Fallback: 7B-quantized model deployed in same region, auto-failover on queue > 200ms
- Prewarm: 10m scheduled before predicted peak
```
alex_sales: Can you map that to estimated monthly cost (order of magnitude) and the billing trigger for burst? They want pricing delta for reserving vs pure on-demand.
olga_support: Also need note about data isolation and VPC options — legal wants explicit statement that no logs are shared.
ian_sre: Quick ops notes: autoscale policy should use multi-signal: queue depth + p95 latency + CPU/GPU util. Set cooldown 90s, max burst duration 15m before throttling. Add cross-AZ fallback to avoid single-AZ outage.
maya_prod: And caching: prefix KV cache for repeated system prompts could shave token spend by ~12-18%. Add caching recommendation to the playbook.
kevin_se: I'll draft a short one-pager: traffic matrix -> recommended reserve count -> burst/autoscale rules -> fallback model -> cost delta. Need exact throughput numbers per GPU for their chosen 30B v 7B quantized — can we ship those numbers?
ian_sre: Use our internal throughput matrix: 30B fp16: ~100 RPS/GPU @80 tokens; 7B int8: ~450 RPS/GPU @80 tokens. I'll attach quick validation note in the runbook.
alex_sales: Perfect. Also they asked about prewarming mechanics — what's the concrete command/approach?
deploy-bot: Scheduled preload job created: `prewarm job atlascorp-poc --model 30B --duration 10m --start 2024-06-03T09:50:00Z`
ian_sre: Prewarm runs synthetic traffic to fill KV caches and spin GPU contexts. Recommend run 10m at 25% of expected burst RPS, and a short steady 5m at full baseline to validate tails.
kevin_se: I'll include sample autoscale YAML for the sales playbook:
```yaml
autoscale_policy:
  - metric: queue_depth
    threshold: 250
    action: add_gpu(2)
  - metric: p95_latency
    threshold_ms: 350
    action: enable_fallback_model
  cooldown: 90s
  max_burst_duration: 15m
```
alex_sales: Great. Final asks from AtlasCorp: 1) hard SLA guarantees, 2) pricing for reserved + burst, 3) security note for VPC. I'll consolidate and send.
olga_support: I'll draft the contractual SLA language and a short security blurb about VPC + KMS + audit logs.
maya_prod: I'll produce the playbook doc and an ops checklist for the POC run (prewarm steps, monitoring dashboards, rollback plan).
kevin_se: Send me the draft before EOD and I'll add the throughput numbers and cost delta.
alex_sales: Thanks team — aiming to share with AtlasCorp tomorrow AM. :rocket:
